plan:
RATIONALE

The question is fundamentally about implementation overhead: which parts of "step the MPE Simple Spread world" dominate wall-clock time when each agent acts once and the world advances once under uniform random actions. Steps-per-second is the natural unit because it is what an MARL practitioner would actually measure when choosing a backend for a rollout-heavy training loop, and it is the unit in which JaxMARL typically documents its throughput claims. Holding hardware fixed (the same 24-core sandbox), fixing the threading model (single-thread as primary, all-cores as secondary), and using a deterministic random-action schedule that is matched in spirit across arms removes the most common confounders — GPU vs CPU, batched vs single-env, and policy cost — so any residual difference is attributable to the algorithmic and data-flow choices made by the two implementations. Reporting both per-agent-action SPS and per-global-tick SPS lets the reader convert to either MARL convention without re-measuring, since one global tick = N agent-action transitions by construction. K = 5 trials and per-trial ratios are deliberately framed as descriptive measurement rather than hypothesis testing; the design characterises the comparison and does not pre-commit a directional claim.

SECTION A — Implementations / arms

All three arms run CPU-only on the same 24-core sandbox. No GPU interaction at any point. One Python process per arm within a single trial loop; no rollout workers.

Arm 1 — PettingZoo MPE simple_spread, parallel API. Primary CPU baseline.
  - Package: pettingzoo.sisl.mpe; env class: simple_spread (latest available variant in the installed source — verify the exact variant identifier, e.g. simple_spread_v3 vs simple_spread, and the matching continuous-action conventions, against the installed source rather than asserting a specific identifier here).
  - Step surface: the parallel API, where one parallel step advances every agent and produces a per-agent observation. This is the closest analogue to a JaxMARL tick and is the baseline for the headline ratio.

Arm 2 — PettingZoo MPE simple_spread, AEC API. Secondary, rules-only line item.
  - Same env class / variant as Arm 1 (verify variant against source).
  - Step surface: the AEC API, in which each env.step call advances a single agent; a full global tick therefore costs N individual AEC step calls plus the implicit agent cycling. Per-step timing in this arm counts N agent-action transitions per global tick, but each transition carries its own Python overhead — this is the structural reason AEC is reported as a separate line item rather than folded into the headline ratio.

Arm 3 — JaxMARL MPE simple_spread. Two sub-lines under one arm.
  - Package: jaxmarl; env id: MPE_simple_spread or equivalent — verify the exact import path and constructor name against the installed source.
  - Sub-line 3a (JAX_single): single-env stepping, where env.step consumes a dict/PyTree of per-agent actions whose shape matches N — verify the expected action container shape against source.
  - Sub-line 3b (JAX_batched): JaxMARL's native batched time-step path, only if the installed module exposes such a wrapper for Simple Spread (verify whether such a wrapper is part of the public JaxMARL API in the installed version; if absent, sub-line 3b is reported as "not present in installed source" rather than fabricated). Both sub-lines execute on the CPU backend with JIT enabled; no GPU dispatch.

SECTION B — Metric definition

Wall-clock time is measured with time.perf_counter() (perf_counter_ns() acceptable).

SPS_agent = total_agent_action_transitions / (t_end − t_start).
SPS_tick  = total_global_ticks         / (t_end − t_start).

Identity (by construction, since one tick yields N agent-action transitions): SPS_tick = SPS_agent / N. The design records a single numerator (agent-action transitions) and a single denominator (timed elapsed), then derives SPS_tick from SPS_agent via the configured N. No second measurement is taken.

Numerator rules:
  - One global tick in any arm counts as N agent-action transitions.
  - reset() calls do NOT count as agent-action transitions and are excluded from both numerators.
  - The terminating done / terminated step call that closes an episode IS counted as N agent-action transitions (it is a real env step); the immediately following reset() is excluded.

Warm-up policy:
  - Discard exactly the first full episode's worth of agent-action transitions (i.e. N × H if the underlying episode terminates at the horizon H — verify term-at-horizon behaviour against source).
  - If N × H < 1000, discard a 1000-transition floor instead. The chosen warm-up budget is recorded as the parameter warmup_transitions and reported alongside every cell.

Reset policy:
  - The timed window strictly excludes reset() calls.
  - During the timed window, compute RPS = num_resets_in_window / (t_end − t_start) and report it as a separate quantity per arm per cell. Intent: verify that RPS is small relative to SPS_tick in both arms (i.e. resets are not the bottleneck). If RPS is comparable to SPS_tick in any arm, flag as an anomaly in the result write-up without re-timing.

SECTION C — Held-fixed controls

Per-run controls (identical across all three arms within a single run):
  - N: number of agents. Selected from the grid below.
  - H: episode horizon. Identical across arms within a run.
  - Render mode: off (no renderer instantiation, no frame draw, no glut/canvas calls).
  - Hot loop: no print, no per-step allocation beyond env return values, no growing list comprehensions, no logging inside the timed loop.
  - Single process; no subprocess workers; no thread-pool beyond what JAX itself creates.

Matched grid (minimum four cells per arm):
  - Cell C1 — "both arms' own defaults": each arm at its own default N and default H (verify each default against source).
  - Cell C2 — "match-1": both arms use identical (N1, H1). Suggested pair (N1 = 3, H1 = 25) is treated as "verify against source; common MPE defaults but not asserted here".
  - Cell C3 — "match-2": both arms use identical (N2, H2), different from C2. Suggested pair (N2 = 6, H2 = 50) — verify (N2, H2) is supported by both envs before measurement.
  - The grid therefore reports at minimum {C1, C2, C3} per arm. C2 and C3 must have the same N and H used across arms within the cell.

Threading:
  - Primary comparison: OMP_NUM_THREADS = 1, MKL_NUM_THREADS = 1, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS = 1, and JAX's CPU thread pool size = 1 (set via the relevant JAX env-var or runtime API — verify the exact setting name against the installed jax version, since JAX has changed its configuration surface across releases). All thread settings applied at process start before any imports where possible.
  - Secondary scaling sub-arm: thread_count = 24 (same env vars set to 24), applied identically to all three arms. Reported separately so the primary ratio is not contaminated by intra-process parallel scaling.

Random-action producer (Section D) feeds every arm; thread settings apply uniformly.

SECTION D — Random-action protocol

  - Sampler: a single numpy.random.default_rng(seed) instance drives action sampling for warm-up plus the timed window. The warm-up consumes a known number of draws, so the timed phase always starts from a deterministic RNG state regardless of warm-up length.
  - Master seed list per cell: [seed_1, seed_2, ..., seed_K]; K = 5 by default. Each seed_k is consumed by all three arms in turn.
  - Action shape and clamping are determined by each arm's own action space; uniform sampling is enforced by the producer via rng.uniform(low = ..., high = ..., size = ...), clipped/rounded into the env's action representation (continuous vs discrete — verify against source for each arm).
  - No learned policy. No manual batching of step invocations beyond what each arm's API forces. AEC is stepped one agent at a time; parallel API one global tick at a time; JadeMARL single-env one global tick at a time; JaxMARL batched in its native batched granularity.
  - On a per-trial basis, the same seed_k is replayed across arms in the order Arm1 → Arm2 → Arm3a → Arm3b (if present), so trial k sees the same action stream in all arms.

SECTION E — Repetition and statistics

  - K = 5 trials per (arm, cell) by default. The trial loop is parameterised by K; the design must allow raising K to e.g. 10 or 20 without code changes — only the seed-list length changes.
  - Trial interleaving: within one Python process, for each trial k in 1..K, run the arms in the order Arm1 → Arm2 → Arm3a → Arm3b on the same seed_k. This shares cache and background state across arms as much as the OS allows.
  - Per cell, per arm, K trials: record t_warmup_end, t_end, num_agent_actions, num_resets_timed. Compute SPS_agent, SPS_tick, RPS.
  - Summary statistics per cell per arm: mean, median, std, min, max of SPS_agent (and equivalently SPS_tick).
  - Variance-reduction statistic: per-trial ratios r_k = SPS_agent_JAX,k / SPS_agent_PZ,k computed separately against the parallel arm and the AEC arm. Aggregate the K per-trial ratios into mean / median / std / min / max as additional summary statistics.
  - A run manifest (text file) records: arms run, cells, K, thread_count, master seed list, warmup_transitions used per arm, the actual jax / pettingzoo / jaxmarl versions imported. No measurement is reported without its manifest.

SECTION F — Analysis plan

  - Primary statistic: per-cell ratio R = SPS_agent_JAX_single / SPS_agent_PZ_parallel, computed per trial and aggregated across the K = 5 trials within that cell. Headline reporting: one R per matched (N, H) cell {C2, C3}, plus one R at each arm's own defaults (C1). Cross-cell summary: geometric mean and median of R across C1, C2, C3.
  - Secondary statistics, same per-trial shape:
      - R_AEC = SPS_agent_JAX_single / SPS_agent_PZ_AEC, per trial, per cell — discloses the AEC-overhead cost.
      - R_batched = SPS_agent_JAX_batched / SPS_agent_JAX_single, per trial, per cell — discloses the marginal value of JaxMARL's batched path on CPU. Reported only if sub-line 3b exists in source.
  - No significance test is pre-specified. The K = 5 sample is for descriptive reporting.
  - Anomalies flagged without re-running the benchmark:
      - RPS comparable to SPS_tick in any arm.
      - Warm-up obviously insufficient (timed-window SPS for the first 20% of the window more than 2× the timed-window SPS for the last 20%).
      - Thread pin not honoured (JAX reports a CPU pool size different from the requested value).

SECTION G — Feasibility

The items below are EXPECTED TO BE TRUE BUT NOT EXECUTED in this design phase. They are smoke-test checks the executor performs before any timed measurement. They are not benchmark results and are not part of the analysis plan.

  1. python3 --version reports 3.12.x.
  2. pip install 'pettingzoo[sisl]' and pip install jaxmarl (or the package name verified against the latest available JaxMARL publish target — verify against public PyPI listing at executor time) complete without error on system Python.
  3. PettingZoo parallel smoke test:
       python3 -c "from pettingzoo.sisl.mpe import simple_spread as ss; \
                   e = ss.parallel_env(); e.reset(); \
                   print(e.step({a: e.action_space(a).sample() for a in e.agents}))"
     exits 0.
  4. PettingZoo AEC smoke test:
       python3 -c "from pettingzoo.sisl.mpe import simple_spread as ss; \
                   e = ss.env(); e.reset(); \
                   [e.step(a) for a in list(e.agent_iter())]; print('ok')"
     exits 0 (adapt as needed to the installed AEC API — verify exact env.reset / agent_iter / step contract against source).
  5. JaxMARL smoke test: import jaxmarl, construct the MPE Simple Spread env module (verify exact import path against source), reset, step once with uniform random actions, exit 0.
  6. CPU and GPU detection:
       python3 -c "import os, multiprocessing; print('cpu_count=', os.cpu_count(), multiprocessing.cpu_count())"
     reports 24 (or 24 logical cores); nvidia-smi is either absent or reports no devices; JAX reports default_backend() == 'cpu'.
  7. JAX thread-pool setting acceptance: the JAX CPU thread-count setting named in Section C accepts the values 1 and 24 (verify the exact setting name against the installed jax version, e.g. XLA_FLAGS vs the runtime API).
  8. Reference thread-pinning shell test:
       OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 JAX_CPU_THREAD_COUNT=1 python3 -c "import jax; print(jax.devices(), jax.local_device_count())"
     runs and the executor confirms the device list contains exactly one CPU device.

If any item above fails, the design's feasibility assumption is violated; the executor reports the failure rather than substituting a workaround.

SECTION H — Out of scope

  - Any GPU execution arm — sandbox is gpu_enabled: false; design's purpose is to compare algorithmic / parsimony differences only.
  - Learned policies, behaviour cloning, or trained-agent rollouts — random uniform actions only.
  - Network I/O, distributed rollout, Ray / Slime / Horovod style multi-node setup.
  - Multi-process or subprocess vectorisation beyond what each arm's native API offers (no custom wrapper loop that calls env.step on a worker pool).
  - Benchmarking on hardware other than the provided 24-core CPU-only sandbox.
  - Significance testing, power analysis, or Bayesian model comparison on the K = 5 sample.
  - Quantitative claims about JaxMARL vs original MPE outside the matched cells actually executed.
  - Invented third-party references, paper citations, or version numbers not verifiable from the installed source.

ASSUMPTIONS AND UNRESOLVED KNOWNS

Assumptions (on which the design rests):
  - Assumption: uniform random actions exercise the dominant per-step compute path of both envs; no policy-dependent branching changes the hot loop.
  - Assumption: one global tick produces N agent-action transitions in both PettingZoo parallel and JaxMARL single-env, and N agent-action transitions spread across N AEC step calls in the AEC arm; the per-arm cardinality is constant within a run.
  - Assumption: thread-pinning via the named environment variables is honoured by NumPy/SciPy-backed env code and by JAX on CPU for the installed jax version.
  - Assumption: the JIT compilation cost in JaxMARL is captured by the warm-up (i.e. it has completed before the timed window begins); this should be verified by inspecting the stability of timed-window SPS across the window.
  - Assumption: SPS is interpreted as a relative comparison of implementations, not as a portable benchmark.
  - Assumption: the 24-core sandbox's CPU frequency and thermal state do not drift appreciably across K = 5 interleaved trials; trial interleaving is the design's primary mitigation, not a guarantee.

Unresolved knowns (each must be confirmed against the installed source before measurement; suggested defaults below are NOT asserted as facts about specific files):
  - Unknown — exact N and H defaults for PettingZoo simple_spread and JaxMARL MPE_simple_spread in the installed versions → verify against source.
  - Unknown — which simple_spread variant (v2 vs v3) is "the original" on the PettingZoo side → verify against source; design specifies "latest available" and tags the identifier for confirmation.
  - Unknown — whether the latest variant exposes continuous or discrete actions by default (often continuous in MPE) → verify against source; design accommodates either via uniform sampling with per-arm range/shape mapping.
  - Unknown — whether the installed jaxmrel release exposes a public batched time-step wrapper for MPE simple_spread → verify against source; sub-line 3b is reported as "not present in installed source" if absent.
  - Unknown — exact JAX CPU thread-count env-var / API name in the installed jax version → verify against source; design pins the thread count by whatever the installed jax version exposes.
  - Unknown — exact import path for jaxmarl environments in the installed version → verify against source.
  - Unknown — exact PettingZoo AEC semantics in the installed simple_spread variant (does e.step(agent) advance only that agent or the whole world?) → verify against source; the agent-action-transition counting handles either by counting one transition per AEC step call.
  - Unknown — expected directional result → do not pre-commit; the design is descriptive.

The question is fundamentally about implementation overhead: which parts of "step the MPE Simple Spread world" dominate wall-clock time when each agent acts once and the world advances once under uniform random actions. Steps-per-second is the natural unit because it is what an MARL practitioner would actually measure when choosing a backend for a rollout-heavy training loop, and it is the unit in which JaxMARL typically documents its throughput claims. Holding hardware fixed (the same 24-core sandbox), fixing the threading model (single-thread as primary, all-cores as secondary), and using a deterministic random-action schedule that is matched in spirit across arms removes the most common confounders — GPU vs CPU, batched vs single-env, and policy cost — so any residual difference is attributable to the algorithmic and data-flow choices made by the two implementations. Reporting both per-agent-action SPS and per-global-tick SPS lets the reader convert to either MARL convention without re-measuring, since one global tick = N agent-action transitions by construction. K = 5 trials and per-trial ratios are deliberately framed as descriptive measurement rather than hypothesis testing; the design characterises the comparison and does not pre-commit a directional claim.

SECTION A — Implementations / arms

All three arms run CPU-only on the same 24-core sandbox. No GPU interaction at any point. One Python process per arm within a single trial loop; no rollout workers.

Arm 1 — PettingZoo MPE simple_spread, parallel API. Primary CPU baseline.
  - Package: pettingzoo.sisl.mpe; env class: simple_spread (latest available variant in the installed source — verify the exact variant identifier, e.g. simple_spread_v3 vs simple_spread, and the matching continuous-action conventions, against the installed source rather than asserting a specific identifier here).
  - Step surface: the parallel API, where one parallel step advances every agent and produces a per-agent observation. This is the closest analogue to a JaxMARL tick and is the baseline for the headline ratio.

Arm 2 — PettingZoo MPE simple_spread, AEC API. Secondary, rules-only line item.
  - Same env class / variant as Arm 1 (verify variant against source).
  - Step surface: the AEC API, in which each env.step call advances a single agent; a full global tick therefore costs N individual AEC step calls plus the implicit agent cycling. Per-step timing in this arm counts N agent-action transitions per global tick, but each transition carries its own Python overhead — this is the structural reason AEC is reported as a separate line item rather than folded into the headline ratio.

Arm 3 — JaxMARL MPE simple_spread. Two sub-lines under one arm.
  - Package: jaxmarl; env id: MPE_simple_spread or equivalent — verify the exact import path and constructor name against the installed source.
  - Sub-line 3a (JAX_single): single-env stepping, where env.step consumes a dict/PyTree of per-agent actions whose shape matches N — verify the expected action container shape against source.
  - Sub-line 3b (JAX_batched): JaxMARL's native batched time-step path, only if the installed module exposes such a wrapper for Simple Spread (verify whether such a wrapper is part of the public JaxMARL API in the installed version; if absent, sub-line 3b is reported as "not present in installed source" rather than fabricated). Both sub-lines execute on the CPU backend with JIT enabled; no GPU dispatch.

SECTION B — Metric definition

Wall-clock time is measured with time.perf_counter() (perf_counter_ns() acceptable).

SPS_agent = total_agent_action_transitions / (t_end − t_start).
SPS_tick  = total_global_ticks         / (t_end − t_start).

Identity (by construction, since one tick yields N agent-action transitions): SPS_tick = SPS_agent / N. The design records a single numerator (agent-action transitions) and a single denominator (timed elapsed), then derives SPS_tick from SPS_agent via the configured N. No second measurement is taken.

Numerator rules:
  - One global tick in any arm counts as N agent-action transitions.
  - reset() calls do NOT count as agent-action transitions and are excluded from both numerators.
  - The terminating done / terminated step call that closes an episode IS counted as N agent-action transitions (it is a real env step); the immediately following reset() is excluded.

Warm-up policy:
  - Discard exactly the first full episode's worth of agent-action transitions (i.e. N × H if the underlying episode terminates at the horizon H — verify term-at-horizon behaviour against source).
  - If N × H < 1000, discard a 1000-transition floor instead. The chosen warm-up budget is recorded as the parameter warmup_transitions and reported alongside every cell.

Reset policy:
  - The timed window strictly excludes reset() calls.
  - During the timed window, compute RPS = num_resets_in_window / (t_end − t_start) and report it as a separate quantity per arm per cell. Intent: verify that RPS is small relative to SPS_tick in both arms (i.e. resets are not the bottleneck). If RPS is comparable to SPS_tick in any arm, flag as an anomaly in the result write-up without re-timing.

SECTION C — Held-fixed controls

Per-run controls (identical across all three arms within a single run):
  - N: number of agents. Selected from the grid below.
  - H: episode horizon. Identical across arms within a run.
  - Render mode: off (no renderer instantiation, no frame draw, no glut/canvas calls).
  - Hot loop: no print, no per-step allocation beyond env return values, no growing list comprehensions, no logging inside the timed loop.
  - Single process; no subprocess workers; no thread-pool beyond what JAX itself creates.

Matched grid (minimum four cells per arm):
  - Cell C1 — "both arms' own defaults": each arm at its own default N and default H (verify each default against source).
  - Cell C2 — "match-1": both arms use identical (N1, H1). Suggested pair (N1 = 3, H1 = 25) is treated as "verify against source; common MPE defaults but not asserted here".
  - Cell C3 — "match-2": both arms use identical (N2, H2), different from C2. Suggested pair (N2 = 6, H2 = 50) — verify (N2, H2) is supported by both envs before measurement.
  - The grid therefore reports at minimum {C1, C2, C3} per arm. C2 and C3 must have the same N and H used across arms within the cell.

Threading:
  - Primary comparison: OMP_NUM_THREADS = 1, MKL_NUM_THREADS = 1, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS = 1, and JAX's CPU thread pool size = 1 (set via the relevant JAX env-var or runtime API — verify the exact setting name against the installed jax version, since JAX has changed its configuration surface across releases). SECTION D — Random-action protocol

  - Sampler: a single numpy.random.default_rng(seed) instance drives action sampling for warm-up plus the timed window. The warm-up consumes a known number of draws, so the timed phase always starts from a deterministic RNG state regardless of warm-up length.
  - Master seed list per cell: [seed_1, seed_2, ..., seed_K]; K = 5 by default. Each seed_k is consumed by all three arms in turn.
  - Action shape and clamping are determined by each arm's own action space; uniform sampling is enforced by the producer via rng.uniform(low = ..., high = ..., size = ...), clipped/rounded into the env's action representation (continuous vs discrete — verify against source for each arm).
  - No learned policy. No manual batching of step invocations beyond what each arm's API forces. AEC is stepped one agent at a time; parallel API one global tick at a time; JadeMARL single-env one global tick at a time; JaxMARL batched in its native batched granularity.
  - On a per-trial basis, the same seed_k is replayed across arms in the order Arm1 → Arm2 → Arm3a → Arm3b (if present), so trial k sees the same action stream in all arms.

SECTION E — Repetition and statistics

  - K = 5 trials per (arm, cell) by default. The trial loop is parameterised by K; the design must allow raising K to e.g. 10 or 20 without code changes — only the seed-list length changes.

  - Per cell, per arm, K trials: record t_warmup_end, t_end, num_agent_actions, num_resets_timed. Compute SPS_agent, SPS_tick, RPS.
  - Summary statistics per cell per arm: mean, median, std, min, max of SPS_agent (and equivalently SPS_tick).

  - Primary statistic: per-cell ratio R = SPS_agent_JAX_single / SPS_agent_PZ_parallel, computed per trial and aggregated across the K = 5 trials within that cell.
